# Session 16 (Opus, on the LAPTOP): verify S14 (themes) + S15 (selling details) together, so nothing else is broken. Then merge.

Repo `c:\Users\Aarushi\Downloads\LaunchWitness` (Windows + Git Bash), Docker Desktop, the Claude key in `.env` (never read or print `.env`). There's no `gh`.
Read only `CLAUDE.md` and the S14/S15 parts of `docs/STATE_FOR_NEXT_SESSION.md` (on the S15 branch). No plan needed; start right away.
**Time budget: about 60 minutes.** Pipe long output through tail. Fix only what fails.

## 0. Protect tomorrow's deploy first (2 minutes)
`git fetch origin`. Tag the last fully verified commit (S13c, `5622ca5`) as **`vps-safe`** and push the tag (`git tag vps-safe 5622ca5 && git push origin vps-safe`).
Report whether PR #15 (S14) is already in `origin/main` and whether PR #16 (S15) is open, with the commit ids.

## 1. Put S14 + S15 together on a local branch
Branch `s16-verify` from `origin/main`. If S14 isn't in main yet, merge the S14 branch (`--no-ff`), then merge the S15 branch (PR #16's branch, `--no-ff`). Resolve
conflicts carefully: don't drop either side's behaviour.

## 2. Run everything (record pass/fail + time for each)
a. Backend suite (`cd backend && ../.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -q | tail -3`). If only the known timing-sensitive `test_s13_scale.py` tests fail under load,
   rerun that file alone.
b. ruff, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`.
c. **Live fixture re-capture** for the S14 theme choices and the S15 food marks (the S14 `--theme-only` command mentioned in the PRs; cap **$0.10**, `CLAUDE_MODE=live`
   only in that command's environment). Then run the suite with `REQUIRE_LIVE_FIXTURES=1` (you can skip the scale file). Report the spend.
d. Docker: `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.local.yml up -d --build --wait` (retry once on the
   Windows file-lock error).
e. `bash scripts/check_m1.sh --local`: every check must pass.
f. **The full e2e suite against the Docker stack** (all flows, old and new: sign-in, practice + real launch, proof hops, "Yes, I got it" where possible, the Doctor's staged
   fault + trace, the symptom box, the receipt verify, Orders + the outbox "retrying → sent", sign-in while mail is down, check any address, watch, photos, landing
   sections, the S15 out-of-area → pickup flow).
g. **Themes in production settings:** for each of the six themes, a shop opens on its shop host over https through Caddy with **no CSP violations or blocked fonts in the
   browser console**, the hidden `lw-shop` marker is present, and one real order goes through the form (Playwright, practice world). Screenshots at 375 and 1440 for
   all six go in `docs/screenshots/s16/`. Look at them yourself; anything visibly broken is a bug.
h. `bash scripts/secret_scan.sh`, and one backup + restore (`LOCAL=1`) with the app healthy after.

## 3. Fix
Every failure in our code: a minimal fix plus a test. An out-of-date test: fix it with a one-line reason. Anything over 15 minutes: don't fix it, write it down.
Don't change behaviour beyond fixing.

## 4. Merge only if green
If **every** step passes: merge `s16-verify` into `main` with `--no-ff`, push main, then re-run step (e) once on main's build. If anything critical is still red, **do not
merge**: push `s16-verify` and report.
Update STATE (one short S16 section: what ran, what's fixed, which commit is safe to deploy), save the transcript (pass its path explicitly on Windows).

## End with ONLY this report
- A table: step | pass/fail | time | notes
- Bugs fixed (one line each) and anything left unfixed
- Live spend
- One line: **"Deploy main on the VPS: YES"** or **"Deploy the vps-safe tag on the VPS, because …"**

Rules: no DNS writes, no purchases, no deploy, no real email (Mailpit and the practice world only). Never print or read `.env`.
</pasted_content id="0ea5">

addedLines: - adhd-study-coach:adhd-study-coach: Your ongoing ADHD-friendly study companion, for any subject. Use this to start a study session, review what's due, learn something new, wrap up and reflect, or check in on your learning patterns. Handles first-time setup automatically — just start talking to it. Say things like "let's study X", "quiz me", "I'm done for today", or "how am I doing lately". (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash, PowerShell)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- review-ready:crash-risk-auditor: Audits a mobile app for stability and quality issues that cause Apple 2.1 (App Completeness) and Google minimum-functionality rejections. Detects unhandled promise rejections, force-unwrap patterns, missing error boundaries, dev-only code in production, hardcoded localhost URLs, broken navigation, missing demo account info, console errors, and other crash/launch-fail risks. Invoke in parallel with other Review Ready auditors during /review-ready:scan. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash)

- review-ready:iap-business-auditor: Audits a mobile app for monetization compliance against Apple App Store Review Guideline 3.1 (In-App Purchase) and Google Play's Monetization & Ads policy. Detects Stripe/PayPal/other external payment SDKs being used for digital goods (causes guaranteed Apple 3.1.1 rejection), missing subscription disclosure, external payment link bypass, and Play Billing requirements. Invoke in parallel with other Review Ready auditors during /review-ready:scan. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash)

- review-ready:metadata-auditor: Audits a mobile app's metadata and configuration for store compliance. Checks bundle identifiers, version numbers, app name length, app icon specifications (1024x1024 no-alpha for iOS, 512x512 for Play, adaptive icon for Android), encryption export compliance, Sign in with Apple requirement (Apple 4.8), target SDK level, 64-bit support, minimum functionality, and Universal Links / app associations. Invoke in parallel with other Review Ready auditors during /review-ready:scan. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash)

- learning-framework:active-recall: Active Recall (Retrieval Practice) — The testing effect by Roediger·Karpicke. Retrieval (re-test) beats re-study for long-term memory. Pitfalls of highlighting·rereading, the generation effect, desirable difficulty.
- learning-framework:chunking: Chunking — Miller's 7±2 short-term memory constraint, expert chunk perception, and chunk-size calibration in learning design. Meaningless individual items → meaningful chunks = expanded processing capacity. The core representational unit of expertise.

- learning-framework:deliberate-practice: Deliberate Practice — Anders Ericsson's theory of deliberate practice. Expertise is forged not by time but by *conditions*: specific goals, immediate feedback, just beyond current limits, intense focus. The '10,000-hour rule' is Gladwell-style hyperbole that Ericsson himself refuted.
- learning-framework:evergreen-notes: Evergreen Notes — Andy Matuschak's digital note-taking practice. Concept-oriented, continuously edited, densely linked, atomic. - learning-framework:feynman-technique: Feynman Technique — a method of revealing gaps in understanding by explaining to a beginner. 4-step protocol (Choose → Teach → Identify gaps → Simplify). ELI5 approach. The fastest tool to break the illusion of competence.
- learning-framework:interleaving: Interleaving — mixing multiple topics and problem types during study. Compared to blocked repetition, short-term performance ↓ but long-term retention and transfer ↑. Bjork's desirable difficulty. Effectiveness demonstrated in math problem types, sports skills, and language training.
- learning-framework:metalearning: Metalearning — Barbara Oakley *Learning How to Learn* + Scott Young *Ultralearning*. Focused/diffuse modes, illusion of competence, MOC (map of content), learning project design. The upper layer for rapidly acquiring new fields.
- learning-framework:pomodoro-and-focus: Pomodoro Technique (Cirillo 25/5) + focus variants (50/10, 90-minute ultradian). Sophie Leroy's attention residue. Train attention muscle through short focus units + timeboxing tool. The implementation layer of Deep Work.
- learning-framework:second-brain-para: Building a Second Brain — Tiago Forte's personal knowledge management system. PARA (Projects/Areas/Resources/Archives) organization + CODE (Capture/Organize/Distill/Express) workflow. Strong on execution-orientation and project linkage. For when you're drowning in information or stuck on where to put what.

# CLAUDE.md — LaunchWitness

Read this file fully at the start of every session. It is the source of truth for how you work in this repo.

## What we are building

LaunchWitness (working name) — GoDaddy Inclusive Innovation Hackathon 2026, Round 2 (build Nov 13–20, 2026).

> Describe your business. LaunchWitness puts it online on GoDaddy, proves a real order reaches you, fixes what breaks, and keeps checking.

A small seller types a few lines + a price list. LaunchWitness builds her site from one fixed template, buys/points her domain, sets up her email, then **proves** it all works (HTTPS, DNS, email records, a real test order arriving in her inbox), repairs or undoes anything that fails during launch, and keeps lightly checking afterwards.

Full product spec: `docs/SPEC.md`. Milestones and acceptance criteria: `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md`.

## Session ritual (every session, no exceptions)

1. **Start:** read `CLAUDE.md`, then `docs/PROGRESS.md` (current milestone, what's done, what's next, open questions). Only read `docs/SPEC.md` / `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md` sections relevant to today's task.
2. **Before coding:** state in 3–6 bullets what you will do this session and which acceptance criteria from `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md` it targets. Wait for the user's OK if the plan changes anything in `docs/SPEC.md`.
3. **While coding:** small commits, each one working. Run tests before every commit.
4. **End:** update `docs/PROGRESS.md` (move items to Done, set Next, add decisions/open questions) and append one entry to `docs/BUILD_LOG.md` (template inside). Then commit.
5. **Save the transcript:** run `bash scripts/save-transcript.sh <N> <milestone>` (e.g. `2 m2`; set `REDACT_EMAILS=<owner's email>` in the shell, never in a file). It copies this session's transcript to `replay/sessions/<date>-s<N>-<milestone>.jsonl`, redacts the owner's personal email (and any webmail address), replaces each secret-looking value with `[REDACTED]` (strict patterns; code like `password: SecretStr` and base64 screenshot data are not flagged), then re-scans. If anything real-looking remains, it saves nothing and exits 1 — **never commit that transcript**; tell the user which lines matched (it prints line numbers and kinds, never values). Commit the saved file only when the script reports a clean scan. `replay/raw/` stays git-ignored.

## Hard rules

- **No secrets anywhere in the repo.** All keys come from environment variables (see `.env.example`). Never print a secret, never write it to a file other than `.env` (which is git-ignored), never paste it into a commit, test, fixture or log. If you see a secret in a file, stop and tell the user.
- **Never spend money.** Do not run any GoDaddy purchase (domain or email) yourself — not via API, not via `gddy`. Purchases are done by the user on godaddy.com with hackathon credit. In code, purchase paths are guarded by `ALLOW_PURCHASE=false` (default) AND a `MAX_SPEND_USD` cap AND an owner approval record. Never change those defaults.
- **GoDaddy environment:** default `GODADDY_ENV=ote` (sandbox). Production calls only when the user sets `GODADDY_ENV=prod` explicitly. Never write DNS to a domain that is not in the app's own database.
- **Claude API budget is $100 total, for the product only.** During development, do not call the live Claude API for UI work: use saved fixtures in `backend/tests/fixtures/`. Live calls only when a task is specifically about the prompt/agent, and keep `max_tokens` tight. Strong model only for the Reader; cheap model for Namer and Doctor (see env vars).
- **The model never acts alone on money or DNS.** Claude only *decides and explains* (Reader, Namer, Doctor). Plain code *acts and checks* (Planner, Executor, Checker). The Doctor may only pick from the fixed playbook in code.
- **Scope:** build the core features in `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md` order. No stretch item until the user says core is done. Out of scope: payments, inventory, WhatsApp/Instagram APIs, multiple templates, generating custom site code.
- **Don't invent product decisions.** If the spec doesn't answer something, pick the simplest option, write it under "Decisions" in `docs/PROGRESS.md`, and mention it in your end-of-session summary.

## Stack

- Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLModel/SQLite, httpx, dnspython, APScheduler, `anthropic` SDK, pytest.
- Frontend: React + Vite + TypeScript, plain CSS (no heavy UI kit).
- Seller sites: server-rendered by FastAPI (Jinja2) from ONE template + the seller's profile, chosen by the `Host` header.
- Infra: one GoDaddy Docker VPS, `docker compose` with `caddy` (HTTPS, on-demand TLS with an `ask` endpoint) + `app` (FastAPI serving API, built frontend and seller sites).
- Email: send via SMTP of the app's one Titan mailbox (`smtpout.secureserver.net`, full address as username, password from env). Read the demo inbox via IMAP (password from env).
- GoDaddy: REST APIs (Domains, DNS, Email) behind one client class, plus `gddy` CLI for manual exploration.

## Repo layout (target)

```
backend/
  app/
    main.py            # FastAPI app, routers, host-based seller site routing
    config.py          # settings from env (pydantic-settings)
    db.py, models.py   # SQLite tables: Business, Plan, DnsBackup, CheckResult, AuditEvent, Approval
    audit.py           # one helper to write AuditEvent rows
    routers/           # health.py (/api/health), internal.py (/internal/tls-ask)
    safety/            # spend_guard.py (ALLOW_PURCHASE + MAX_SPEND_USD + Approval)
    checks/            # dns_resolver.py (public DNS lookups, real + fake)
    agents/            # claude_client.py (fixture|live); reader.py, namer.py, doctor.py (Claude); planner.py, executor.py, checker.py, playbook.py (code)
    integrations.py    # bundle of outside services (fake world or real), FastAPI dependency
    godaddy/           # client.py (ote|prod, scoped DNS writes), availability.py, email.py (mailbox)
    sites/             # templates/seller.html, render.py, hosts.py, routes.py, orders.py
    monitor/           # scheduler.py (light monitoring)
    mail/              # smtp.py, imap.py
  tests/               # pytest; fixtures/ holds saved Claude responses + sample seller inputs
frontend/              # Vite React app
deploy/                # Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, Caddyfile (local), Caddyfile.prod
docs/                  # SPEC.md, BUILD_PLAN.md, PROGRESS.md, BUILD_LOG.md
scripts/               # build-replay.sh and helpers
```

## Commands (keep this section updated as they become real)

- One-time setup: `cp .env.example .env` · `python3.12 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt` · `cd frontend && npm install`
- Backend tests: `cd backend && ../.venv/bin/pytest -q` (or `pytest -q` with `.venv` activated). Tests block all non-local network calls.
- Backend only (dev): `cd backend && ../.venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000`
- Frontend dev: `cd frontend && npm run dev` (proxies `/api` to :8000) · build: `npm run build` (FastAPI serves `frontend/dist`)
- Run locally (full stack): `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build` → http://localhost · stop: `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml down`
- Practice mode: `USE_FAKES=true` (default) runs GoDaddy/DNS/mailbox/HTTP against in-memory fakes; set `SERVER_IP`, `USE_FAKES=false` on the VPS once the real integrations exist (see PROGRESS.md "Real integration TODO").
- Live Claude fixtures (owner's laptop; cloud sessions can't hold the key): `bash scripts/capture_all_live.sh` (17 calls, worst case $0.14, cap must be ≤ $1.50, stops at the first failure; details `docs/LIVE_FIXTURES.md`). Single targets: `cd backend && ../.venv/bin/python ../scripts/capture_live_fixtures.py [--dry-run] reader:<seller> | namer:<seller> | doctor:<check>|all` · spend today: `… --report` · strict check: `REQUIRE_LIVE_FIXTURES=1 pytest -q tests/test_s6_agents.py`. Handwritten test image: `.venv/bin/python scripts/make_handwritten_pricelist.py <out.jpg>`
- Accounts: sign in by email link at `/#/signin` (local: `DEV_MODE=true` shows the link on screen; never on https). The `ADMIN_EMAIL` user is the team: `/#/admin` (approve accounts, pause shops, reports) and the demo fault switch on reports. `ADMIN_TOKEN` (16+ chars) is for command-line tools only (`X-Admin-Token`, no cookies). Every route must be listed in `backend/app/safety/route_table.py` (a test enforces it).
- Live pre-flight (S11c): `cd backend && CLAUDE_MODE=live ../.venv/Scripts/python ../scripts/preflight_live.py [reader|reader:<id>] [namer] [policy] [doctor]` (app routes + live Claude on a scratch DB, cap $0.25/day) · real DNS write-and-undo, **only with the owner's OK each time**: `… ../scripts/preflight_dns_write.py --yes-owner-approved`
- `DNS_MODE=per_shop` (default: one A record per shop) | `wildcard` (owner made `*` by hand; the app reads/writes no shop DNS). `docs/NEXT_SESSION_VPS.md` "If GoDaddy's API refuses us".
- Monitoring: on by default (`MONITOR_ENABLED=true`, starts with the app); tests never start it.
- Save session transcript: `bash scripts/save-transcript.sh <N> <milestone>` · build replay page: `REDACT_EMAILS=<owner email> bash scripts/build-replay.sh` → `replay/build.html` (served at `/build`; redacts emails, secret-scans the page, deletes it on any hit). One Claude Code session = one file in `replay/sessions/` (the replay keeps one copy per session id: if a chat continues, replace its earlier partial file).
- **Production-like stack locally** (HTTPS via Caddy's local CA, `DEV_MODE=false`, fakes, Mailpit at :8025, never reads `.env`): `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.local.yml up -d --build --wait` → https://launchwitness.localhost · checks: `bash scripts/check_m1.sh --local` · details `deploy/README.md`
- E2E (Playwright, 16 flows; S12 flows in `e2e/tests/h-s12.spec.ts`, S13 outbox flows in `e2e/tests/i-s13.spec.ts` (the sign-in one stops/starts the Mailpit container: Docker stack only, skipped otherwise); `LW_CHROME=<path>` uses a pre-installed Chromium): `cd e2e && npm install && npx playwright install chromium && npx playwright test` (Docker stack) or `LW_BASE=http://localhost:8000 LW_MAIL= npx playwright test` (dev server) · `e2e/README.md` · screenshots: `npx playwright test -c screens.config.ts s105` (owner flow → `docs/screenshots/s10-5/`) or `… s105b` (landing → `docs/screenshots/s10-5b/`), `… s12` (S12 report/landing/photos at 375/1440/1917 + a recording → `docs/screenshots/s12/`), `LW_SHOTS=<dir>` to redirect
- Secret scan of the repo + whole git history (values never printed): `bash scripts/secret_scan.sh` · security overview `docs/SECURITY.md`
- **VPS day: `docs/NEXT_SESSION_VPS.md`** (supersedes the order in `docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md`). One app process only (the app refuses a second). DB backup: `bash scripts/backup_db.sh` (7 daily + 4 weekly) · restore: `bash scripts/restore_db.sh <file>`.
- Prod on the VPS: follow `docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md`. Start/update: `docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build` (Caddyfile.prod, monitoring on, restart always, healthchecks) · M1 check: `bash scripts/check_m1.sh`
- Demo rehearsal (practice, needs the app running, `ADMIN_TOKEN` in env): `python3 scripts/seed_demo.py [--url URL] [--launched]` · reset: `python3 scripts/seed_demo.py --reset`
- Lint: `.venv/Scripts/python -m ruff check backend` (rules pinned in `backend/pyproject.toml`). On Windows use `.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest` (pytest.exe is blocked).
- **Shop themes (S14)**: `backend/app/sites/themes.py` (six themes, accents, rule-based choice, contrast helpers), `templates/seller.html` + `templates/css/` + `templates/art/`, fonts `backend/app/sites/fonts/` (`docs/FONTS.md`, rebuild: `scripts/build_theme_fonts.py`). Screenshots of every theme: `.venv/bin/python scripts/render_theme_shots.py <tmp> && node scripts/shoot_themes.js <tmp> docs/screenshots/s14 && .venv/bin/python scripts/theme_contact_sheet.py docs/screenshots/s14` (owner's look picker: `cd e2e && npx playwright test -c screens.config.ts s14`). Re-capture the theme fields of the Reader fixtures live (laptop only): `cd backend && CLAUDE_MODE=live ../.venv/bin/python ../scripts/capture_live_fixtures.py --theme-only reader:themes` (cap <= $0.10; `--dry-run` first). Claude only picks keys; code draws.
- **Where she sells / payment (S15)**: rules in `backend/app/sites/fulfilment.py`; tests `tests/test_s15_selling.py`; e2e `e2e/tests/k-s15.spec.ts`; screenshots `.venv/bin/python scripts/render_s15_shots.py <tmp> && node scripts/shoot_s15.js <tmp> docs/screenshots/s15`. Reader food marks/allergens are placeholders until `--theme-only` re-capture (STATE).
- Seller site gallery (6 very different sellers, phone + laptop screenshots): `.venv/bin/python scripts/render_site_gallery.py <tmp_dir> && node scripts/shoot_site_gallery.js <tmp_dir> docs/screenshots/<session>` (warns on sideways scrolling)
- App pages: `/` landing + contact form + "Check any address" (`#check`) · `/#/new` describe (signed in) · `/#/try` describe (guest practice) · `/#/signin[?next=]` · `/#/shops` · `/#/b/<id>` review · `/#/b/<id>/launch` name · `/#/b/<id>/plan/<pid>` approve · `/#/b/<id>/report` · `/#/b/<id>/orders` · `/#/account` · `/#/admin` team · `/#/got-it?token=` ("Yes, I got it") · `/r/<token>` shared report · `/demo/meera|imran|sunita` demo shops · `/build` replay
- S12: product photos `app/photos.py` (Pillow, WebP ×2, stored in SQLite, `/photos/<name>-<w>.webp`); incident timeline `app/incidents.py`; "Describe the problem" `POST /api/businesses/{id}/describe-problem`; staged faults `a_record|marker|cert|smtp_login` on the report's demo switch; S12 Doctor fixtures: `… capture_doctor_investigation.py --s12` (cap $0.10).
- Go-live checklist (S10.5): `app/golive.py`; only real launches are gated. Tests use `tests/conftest.py::ready_for_real`, e2e `helpers.readyForReal`.
- Proof chain: every report claim comes from `Evidence` rows (`app/proof.py`); the checker reaches shops only through `shop_web` (in-process for practice, `SafeWeb` SSRF guard otherwise). Evidence is a per-shop hash chain, append-only (`app/chain.py`; write only through `proof.add`; public check `GET /r/<token>/verify`). Handoff for the next session: `docs/STATE_FOR_NEXT_SESSION.md`.

## Style

- Small, readable modules; type hints; no clever abstractions.
- Every external call (GoDaddy, Claude, SMTP, IMAP, DNS) goes through one wrapper that can be faked in tests.
- Every action that changes state writes an `AuditEvent` (who/what/when/result).
- User-facing text is plain English a non-technical shop owner understands. No "MX", "A record" etc. in the seller UI — technical detail goes in an expandable "details" area.
- Commit messages: imperative, short, prefixed by milestone, e.g. `M2: add DNS backup before writes`.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.
